title: Expressions, functions and terraform console
summary: Conditionals, for expressions (with filters and grouping), splats, the functions you use weekly, templatefile, and trying all of it live in terraform console.

steps.title: Expressions that shape data
body: Most real Terraform code is turning one shape of data into another: a map of services into DNS records, a list of
subnets into security group rules. The tools:
```hcl
locals {
# conditional
instance_type = var.env == "prod" ? "m7g.large" : "t4g.small"
# for expression: list in, list out (with a filter)
web_names = [for name, s in var.servers : upper(name) if s.role == "web"]
# for expression: map out
ip_by_name = { for name, s in var.servers : name => s.ip }
# grouping: the ... collects every value for a repeated key into a list
names_by_role = { for name, s in var.servers : s.role => name... }
# splat: one attribute from every element
subnet_ids = aws_subnet.app[*].id
A `for` over a **map** visits the keys in lexical (sorted) order, so the output is stable from run to run. That
matters: an order that changes between plans means a perpetual diff.

code: > { for name, s in { web-2 = "web", db-1 = "db", web-1 = "web" } : s => name... }
steps.explain: Keys are visited sorted (`db-1`, `web-1`, `web-2`), so each group is in key order. Without the `...`, two entries with the key `"web"` would be an error: *Duplicate object key*.

steps.title: Functions you use every week
body: | Function | Example | Gives |
| `merge` | `merge(local.tags, { Name = "web" })` | one map, later keys win |
| `lookup` | `lookup(var.sizes, var.env, "small")` | a map value with a default |
| `try` | `try(var.settings.tls.min_version, "1.2")` | the first expression that does not error |
| `coalesce` | `coalesce(var.name_override, local.default_name)` | the first non-null, non-empty value |
| `format` | `format("%s-%03d", "web", 7)` | `"web-007"` |
| `join` / `split` | `join(",", var.cidrs)` | text from a list, and back |
| `toset` | `toset(var.names)` | a set, for `for_each` |
| `flatten` | `flatten([for s in var.subnets : s.rules])` | one flat list from nested lists |
| `jsonencode` / `yamlencode` | `jsonencode({ a = 1 })` | `{"a":1}` |
| `templatefile` | `templatefile("${path.module}/nginx.conf.tftpl", { port = 443 })` | a rendered file |
Try anything against your real configuration and state with **`terraform console`**: it evaluates expressions with
your variables, locals and resource attributes. `echo 'local.ip_by_name' | terraform console` works in scripts.
There are no user-defined functions in Terraform (OpenTofu and Terraform 1.8+ support *provider-defined*
functions, called as `provider::NAME::FUNCTION(...)`).

steps.prompt: Match the expression to its result.

steps.title: A hosts file and two outputs from one map
prompt: `~/infra/hosts/variables.tf` has a map of servers (name to IP and role). In `main.tf`, write:
1. a `local_file` at `out/hosts` with one line per server, in name order, `IP NAME.internal.example.com`, ending in a
2. an output `web_ips`: the IPs of the `web` servers, in name order.
3. an output `names_by_role`: a map from each role to the list of its server names.
Try your expressions in `terraform console` first (`var.servers`, then build up the `for`). Then apply.

checks.name: the hosts file is right
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/hosts && diff <(printf '%s\n' '10.20.3.31 cache-1.internal.example.com' '10.20.2.21 db-1.internal.example.com' '10.20.1.11 web-1.internal.example.com' '10.20.1.12 web-2.internal.example.com' '10.20.1.13 web-3.internal.example.com') out/hosts
checks.fail: `out/hosts` should have five lines in name order, `IP NAME.internal.example.com`, and end with a newline (the diff shows what differs).

checks.name: web_ips
checks.fail: `terraform output -json web_ips` should be the three web IPs in name order.

checks.name: names_by_role
checks.fail: `terraform output -json names_by_role` should map each role to its names. A grouping `for` with `...` does it.

checks.name: plan is clean
checks.fail: Apply your changes: `terraform plan` should show none.

hints: `echo '[for name, s in var.servers : "${s.ip} ${name}.internal.example.com"]' | terraform console` shows the lines. `join("\n", ...)` makes them one text; add a final `\n`.
`web_ips`: `[for name, s in var.servers : s.ip if s.role == "web"]`. `names_by_role`: `{ for name, s in var.servers : s.role => name... }`.
solution: value = [for name, s in var.servers : s.ip if s.role == "web"]
value = { for name, s in var.servers : s.role => name... }
steps.explain: One source of truth (the map) feeds a file and two outputs; add a server once and all three follow. For a longer file, `templatefile("hosts.tftpl", { servers = var.servers })` with `%{ for name, s in servers ~}` directives keeps the layout readable.

steps.prompt: `var.settings` may or may not have a `tls` key, and `tls` may or may not have `min_version`. Which expression gives `"1.2"` when either is missing, without an error?
steps.explain: `try` evaluates each argument and returns the first that does not raise an error, so a missing key at any depth falls through to the default. `coalesce` still evaluates `var.settings.tls.min_version` first and errors when `tls` is missing. HCL has no `??` operator.
